subtopics.name: Understanding the Statement of Financial Position

parts.problem_md:
**Extract:**

**Safari Adventures (SA) **

Tokumbo is a sole trader. He started SA 2 years ago in country X. Tokumbo had previously worked for a company selling holidays. SA organises safari tours which take tourists to view wild animals on a game reserve. Most of SA’s customers are tourists from other countries. Tokumbo did not have any objectives when he started SA but knows they are important for his business.

SA uses its own vehicles for the 7 day safari tours and provides accommodation in small local hotels. Tokumbo employs 4 safari guides, 1 for each of the 4 vehicles. The safari guides drive the tourists around the game reserve. There is 1 additional employee who helps Tokumbo in the office with administration. Tokumbo thinks SA needs a website so tourists can book directly with them rather than booking through holiday companies that charge SA a fee.

Tokumbo is considering the following three options for the future growth of SA safari tours:

- Option 1 - increasing the number of safari guides and vehicles to increase the number of customers from the existing target market
- Option 2 – targeting young people who want to camp and sleep in a tent on their safari
- Option 3 - targeting high-income tourists who prefer to stay in luxury hotels

Information about these three options is outlined in Appendix 3.

Tokumbo plans to provide more training for his employees whichever option he chooses. He wants his existing employees to have a wider knowledge of the wild animals on the game reserve and to be able to provide high-quality customer service. Tokumbo has to decide which method of training to use.

**Appendix 1 **

**Newspaper article in Main News, September 2022 **

**Tourism takes off**

Country X is becoming a popular holiday destination for tourists from other countries.

There is an increased demand from high-income tourists who want to stay in luxury hotels whilst on safari tours. These tourists are willing to pay high prices. There is also a new trend for younger people who want cheaper holidays. They prefer to camp and sleep in tents on game reserves rather than stay in hotels.

Are the many safari businesses in country X ready to target these new markets?

The use of e-commerce to find and book safari tours by tourists from other countries is offering both opportunities and threats to businesses in country X.

The inflation rate in country X has increased to 4% which may affect some of our local safari businesses.

**Appendix 2 **

**Email from Tokumbo’s accountant**

To: Tokumbo

From: Accountant

Subject: Source of finance for the new vehicles

New vehicles will be needed whichever option you choose for the future growth of your business.

I have considered several sources of finance you could use for the new vehicles. Interest rates on bank loans have fallen to 2% whilst interest rates on savings are 3%. I think you should choose from one of the following sources:

- Leasing
- Bank loan
- Retained profit

We can meet to discuss these sources if that would help you to decide.

**Appendix 3 **

**SA’s three options for a 7 day safari tour**

|   | Option 1 More existing safari tours | Option 2 Camping safari tours | Option 3 Luxury safari tours |
|---|---|---|---|
| Forecast number of tourists per week | 16 | 32 | 10 |
| Total costs per week for SA to provide these safari tours | \$12 000 | \$8000 | \$20 000 |
| Average cost per tourist | \$750 | ? | ? |
| Price per tourist | \$1000 | \$400 | \$2400 |

Consider the advantages and disadvantages of three sources of finance mentioned in the appendix that Tokumbo could use for his safari business expansion:

- Leasing
- Bank loan
- Retained profit

Which source of finance would have the most significant impact on the statement of financial position? **Justify** your answer.

Refer to the following [insert ](https://cdn.savemyexams.com/uploads/2024/09/nov-2022-paper-21-case-study---new.pdf)[ ](https://cdn.savemyexams.com/uploads/2024/09/nov-2021-paper-2-case-study---new.pdf)when answering the question.
parts.solution_md:
A bank loan gives quick access to money for buying safari vehicles and equipment **[Ap]**. On the balance sheet, the loan appears as a non-current liability, while the new vehicles and equipment are shown as non-current assets **[Ap]**. Fixed monthly repayments make it easier to plan cash flow **[An]**. However, interest increases expenses and reduces profit margins **[An]**. Collateral may also be required, which puts assets at risk if repayments are missed **[An]**

Share capital does not need repayment, so it helps cash flow for daily operations **[Ap]**. On the balance sheet, it increases the equity section, showing that investors now own a share of the business **[An]**. No interest means more profit can be kept for reinvestment **[An]**. However, selling shares reduces Tokumbo’s control over decisions **[Ap]**. Shareholders may also expect dividends, which could reduce money available for growth **[An]**

Using retained earnings has no cost or interest, so more profit is kept in the business **[Ap]**. On the balance sheet, profits are transferred within the equity section, without increasing liabilities **[An]**. Tokumbo keeps full ownership and control **[An]**. However, the amount available is limited, which may restrict expansion [An]. Using these funds also reduces cash reserves, which may cause problems in slow seasons **[An]**

A bank loan would make the biggest change overall to the statement of financial position** [E]**. It increases both liabilities and assets, creating the largest impact on the balance sheet** [E]**. Share capital only affects equity, while retained earnings just move within equity. A loan would also increase gearing, changing SA’s financial structure** [Ap]**

> **[mark-scheme]**
> **Structure**
> 
> - Write one PEA paragraph for each source of finance identified in the question:
> - Point: Identify the source of finance
> - Evidence (Ap): Apply case study detail
> - Analysis (An): Explain business impact
> - Add a final Evaluation (E):
> 
>   - Decide which source has the most significant impact on statement of financial position
>   - Justify your choice
>   - Compare and reject alternatives
> 
> **Marking approach**
> 
> - This is a levelled response answer in which the examiner determines how well you have demonstrated skills of application, analysis and evaluation
> 
>   - Application (4) – Use case study facts
>   - Analysis (4) – Chain effects clearly, using business terms
>   - Evaluation (4) – Balanced judgement, rejects others with reasoning
> 
> **Mark scheme**
> 
> - **Bank loan**
> 
>   - **Advantages**
>   
>     - Immediate access to large amounts → can purchase multiple safari vehicles quickly
>     - Interest payments are tax deductible → reduces overall tax burden
>     - Fixed repayment schedule → predictable cash flow planning
>   - **Disadvantages**
>   
>     - Interest payments increase expenses → reduces net profit margins
>     - Collateral requirements → business assets at risk if cannot repay
> - **Share capital**
> 
>   - **Advantages**
>   
>     - No repayment obligations → improves cash flow for operations
>     - New shareholders bring expertise → potential business growth opportunities
>     - No interest costs → more profit available for reinvestment
>   - **Disadvantages**
>   
>     - Ownership dilution → Tokumbo loses some control over decisions
>     - Dividend expectations → pressure to distribute rather than reinvest profits
>     - Potential conflicts → disagreements over business direction
> - **Retained earnings**
> 
>   - **Advantages**
>   
>     - No external costs → maximises profit retention for expansion
>     - Maintains full ownership → Tokumbo keeps complete control
>     - No debt obligations → reduces financial risk
>   - **Disadvantages**
>   
>     - Limited amount available → may restrict expansion plans
>     - Reduces cash reserves → affects liquidity during quiet periods
>     - Slower expansion → competitors may gain market advantage
> - **Conclusion**
> 
>   - Bank loan creates largest balance sheet impact through simultaneous increase in liabilities and assets
>   - Share capital only affects equity section with smaller overall impact
>   - Retained earnings transfers within equity with minimal net effect on statement of financial position

parts.problem_md: **Explain four** reasons why current assets are important to a business.
parts.solution_md:
Current assets provide liquidity for day-to-day operations **[K]**. Businesses need cash and assets that can be quickly converted to cash to pay suppliers, wages, and other immediate expenses **[An]**

Secondly, current assets enable businesses to meet short-term obligations **[K]**. Having sufficient current assets ensures that a business can pay its current liabilities as they fall due, maintaining good relationships with creditors **[An]**

Current assets also support business flexibility and opportunities **[K]**. Having readily available resources allows businesses to respond quickly to unexpected opportunities or challenges without needing external financing **[An]**

Finally, current assets act as a buffer against financial difficulties **[K]**. Maintaining adequate levels of current assets helps businesses survive temporary downturns in revenue or unexpected expenses **[An]**

> **[mark-scheme]**
> - In your answer:
> 
>   - Give four valid reasons related to the question → 4 K marks
>   - For each reason, explain how or why it matters using a cause–effect link → 4 An marks
> 
> **Mark scheme**
> 
> - Relevant answers might also include:
> 
>   - Current assets support working capital management – proper levels help maintain the cash conversion cycle and operational efficiency
>   - Current assets facilitate growth – having liquid resources available enables businesses to invest in expansion opportunities without delay

parts.problem_md: Do you think maintaining adequate working capital is always essential for a business's long-term success? **Justify** your answer.
parts.solution_md:
Maintaining adequate working capital is crucial for business success as it ensures the company can meet its short-term obligations and maintain smooth operations **[K]**. Without sufficient working capital, businesses may face cash flow crises, struggle to pay suppliers and employees on time, and miss growth opportunities, which could ultimately lead to business failure **[An]**

However, some businesses might deliberately operate with minimal working capital to maximise efficiency and returns. Companies with very predictable cash flows, such as subscription-based businesses, might keep working capital low to invest more in growth or return money to shareholders **[K]**. This approach can increase profitability and demonstrate efficient capital management, particularly when the business has access to credit facilities for emergencies **[An]**

Overall, I believe maintaining adequate working capital is essential for long-term business success **[E]**. While some businesses can operate efficiently with lower working capital, the security and flexibility that adequate working capital provides generally outweighs the potential benefits of operating with minimal reserves, especially given the unpredictable nature of business environments **[E]**

> **[mark-scheme]**
> - You are writing a mini-argument with a decision
> 
>   - Give one relevant reason to support your view → 1 K mark
>   - Explain why this reason affects the business (cause-effect chain) → 1 An mark
>   - Give a different possible reason or viewpoint → 1 K mark
>   - Explain why this could also affect the business → 1 An mark
>   - Make a decision — which argument is stronger or more important overall? → up to 2 E marks
> 
> **Mark scheme**
> 
> - Points might include
> 
>   - Adequate working capital ensures operational stability [k] → enables timely payment of suppliers and employees, maintaining business relationships and avoiding operational disruptions [an]
>   - Provides financial flexibility for opportunities [k] → allows businesses to take advantage of bulk purchase discounts, invest in growth opportunities, or weather unexpected downturns [an]
>   - Some businesses can operate efficiently with minimal working capital [k] → predictable cash flows and access to credit facilities can reduce the need for large working capital reserves [an]
>   - Low working capital maximises capital efficiency [k] → reduces idle cash and can increase return on assets, demonstrating effective capital management to investors [an]
> - Supported judgement might include
> 
>   - Essential for long-term success [e] → the security and flexibility provided by adequate working capital typically outweighs efficiency gains from minimal reserves [e]
>   - Depends on business model and industry [e] → while some businesses can operate with lower working capital, most benefit from maintaining adequate reserves for stability [e]

parts.problem_md: Do you think having more current liabilities than current assets is always a problem for a growing business? **Justify** your answer.
parts.solution_md:
Having more current liabilities than current assets can indicate serious cash flow problems for a growing business. This means the business may struggle to pay its short-term debts like supplier payments and wages **[K]**. This could lead to suppliers refusing to provide goods on credit and employees leaving, which would disrupt operations and damage the business's reputation **[An]**

However, some growing businesses might temporarily have this situation during expansion phases. They might be investing heavily in stock or have large orders coming in soon **[K]**. If the business has strong sales growth and reliable customers who will pay quickly, this temporary imbalance might be manageable and could lead to higher profits once the expansion is complete **[An]**

Overall, I think having more current liabilities than current assets is usually a serious problem for growing businesses **[E]**. While there might be short-term situations where this is acceptable, the risk of not being able to pay bills and the potential damage to relationships with suppliers and employees generally outweighs any temporary benefits from rapid expansion **[E]**

> **[mark-scheme]**
> - You are writing a mini-argument with a decision
> 
>   - Give one relevant reason to support your view → 1 K mark
>   - Explain why this reason affects the business (cause-effect chain) → 1 An mark
>   - Give a different possible reason or viewpoint → 1 K mark
>   - Explain why this could also affect the business → 1 An mark
>   - Make a decision — which argument is stronger or more important overall? → up to 2 E marks
> 
> **Mark scheme**
> 
> - Points might include
> 
>   - Poor working capital position damages business relationships [k] → suppliers may refuse credit terms and employees may leave, harming the business's reputation and operations [an]
>   - Growing businesses may temporarily have this situation during expansion [k] → heavy investment in stock or large pending orders could create temporary imbalances that resolve once growth materialises [an]
>   - Strong sales growth can offset liquidity concerns [k] → if customers pay quickly and sales are increasing, the business may generate enough cash flow to manage the short-term imbalance [an]
>   - Cash flow problems reduce business flexibility [k] → inability to pay bills on time limits opportunities for further growth and may force the business to accept unfavourable terms [an]
> - Supported judgement might include
> 
>   - Usually a serious problem [e] → the risks of operational disruption and damaged relationships typically outweigh temporary expansion benefits [e]
>   - Acceptable only in very specific circumstances [e] → such as when there are guaranteed large payments coming in soon and strong customer relationships [e]

Non-current assets, such as vehicles or property, are items owned by a business **[K] **that will be used for a year or more **[K]**

parts.problem_md:
**Extract:**

**Tasty Tapas Restaurant Chain**

Tasty Tapas is a chain of 10 tapas restaurants in Country Z, established in 2010. The business is owned by Maria and Carlos Rodriguez, who started with one restaurant and gradually expanded. Tasty Tapas is known for its authentic Spanish cuisine and lively atmosphere. The restaurants are popular with both locals and tourists, especially in the evenings and on weekends.

In 2023, Tasty Tapas reported the following financial information:

- Revenue: \$5,000,000
- Gross profit: \$2,000,000
- Profit: \$500,000

Maria and Carlos are considering expanding the business by opening five new restaurants in neighbouring Country Y. This expansion would require an investment of \$2,000,000. They are exploring various financing options, including taking out a new loan, issuing shares to become a private limited company, or using a combination of retained earnings and a bank loan.

However, the restaurant industry in Country Y is highly competitive, with several established chains already operating there. Additionally, there are concerns about potential changes in import tariffs between Country Z and Country Y, which could affect the cost of importing authentic Spanish ingredients.

The owners must also consider the impact of the expansion on their current operations, including the need for additional management staff and the potential strain on their supply chain. They are aware that maintaining consistent quality across all locations will be crucial for the success of the expanded business.

**Appendix 1: Tasty Tapas Statement of Financial Position as of December 31, 2023 (\$000)**

| Non-current assets | 800 |
|---|---|
| Current assets | 400 |
| - Inventory | 200 |
| - Receivables | 50 |
| - Cash | 150 |
| Total assets | 1200 |
| Current liabilities | 300 |
| - Payables | 200 |
| - Short-term loans | 100 |
| Non-current liabilities | 500 |
| Owners capital | 400 |

Consider how each of the following three factors from Tasty Tapas' Statement of Financial Position could affect the decision to expand into Country Y.

- Non-current assets of \$800,000
- Current ratio of 1.33
- Long-term loan of \$500,000

Which factor is likely to have the greatest impact on the expansion decision? **Justify **your answer.

Refer to the following [insert ](https://cdn.savemyexams.com/uploads/2024/10/tasty-tapas-case-study.pdf)when answering the question
parts.solution_md:
Tasty Tapas has non-current assets of \$800,000, such as restaurant buildings and kitchen equipment **[Ap]**, which shows it has a solid foundation. However, expanding into Country Y would require significant investment in new assets, as they may not be enough to support expansion while maintaining current operations **[An]**

The current ratio of 1.33 indicates Tasty Tapas' short-term financial health. It shows the company has \$1.33 in current assets for every \$1 of current liabilities **[Ap]**, which is not very high. Expanding into a new country is risky and could strain Tasty Tapas' ability to pay short-term debts if unexpected costs arise **[An]**

The \$500,000 long-term loan is a significant liability. Taking on more debt to fund expansion could be risky, especially with existing loan commitments. However, it shows Tasty Tapas has been able to secure substantial financing in the past **[Ap]**, so may be able to persuade lenders that it is capable of paying back debts **[An]**

The current ratio will have the greatest impact on the expansion decision **[E]**. Non-current assets, while substantial, are less crucial as they don't directly affect the company's ability to fund the expansion **[E]**. The long-term loan, is less immediate of a concern than the current ratio, as it relates to long-term debts rather than the short-term liquidity needed for expansion **[E]**. The relatively low current ratio suggests Tasty Tapas may not have enough flexibility to safely expand into such a highly competitive market **[Ap] **at this time **[E]**

> **[mark-scheme]**
> **Structure**
> 
> - Write one PEA paragraph for each point identified in the question:
> 
>   - Point: Identify the problem
>   - Evidence (Ap): Apply case study detail
>   - Analysis (An): Explain business impact
> - Add a final Evaluation (E):
> 
>   - Decide which problem is easiest/hardest to overcome
>   - Justify your choice
>   - Compare and reject alternatives
> 
> **Marking approach**
> 
> - This is a levelled response answer in which the examiner determines how well you have demonstrated skills of application, analysis and evaluation
> 
>   - Application (4) – Use case study facts
>   - Analysis (4) – Chain effects clearly, using business terms
>   - Evaluation (4) – Balanced judgement, rejects others with reasoning
> 
> **Mark scheme**
> 
> - **Non-current assets of \$800,000**
> 
>   - **Advantages**
>   
>     - High non-current assets provide credibility for lenders or investors when seeking the \$2m expansion finance
>     - Reflects long-term investment in property and equipment that could be leveraged or sold to fund new restaurants
>   - **Disadvantages**
>   
>     - Assets are illiquid and cannot be quickly converted to cash in a downturn
>     - Ties up capital in existing locations rather than new market entry
> - **Current ratio of 1.33**
> 
>   - **Advantages**
>   
>     - Current assets (\$400,000) exceed current liabilities (\$300,000) by \$100,000 → demonstrates ability to cover short-term obligations during expansion
>     - Positive working capital supports cash-flow needs of opening new sites
>   - **Disadvantages**
>   
>     - Ratio only marginally above the 1 benchmark → limited buffer if cash outflows spike
>     - Includes \$200,000 inventory and \$50,000 receivables that may not convert to cash immediately
> - **Long-term loan of \$500,000**
> 
>   - **Advantages**
>   
>     - Existing debt facility shows prior lender confidence → may ease approval for additional borrowing
>     - Servicing track record could attract favourable terms for further loans
>   - **Disadvantages**
>   
>     - Adds to gearing → limits capacity to take on the additional \$2m debt for Country Y
>     - Interest payments increase fixed costs and reduce cash available for new sites
> - **Conclusion**
> 
>   - Non-current assets back borrowing capacity but lack liquidity for immediate expansion needs
>   - Current ratio indicates workable liquidity yet offers only a small safety margin
>   - Existing long-term loan has the greatest impact by constraining further debt finance and raising fixed interest commitments
>   - Recommendation: address the debt burden first (e.g. pay down or refinance) before committing to the \$2m expansion to preserve financial flexibility

parts.problem_md: Do you think having a high level of non-current liabilities is always a problem for a growing business? **Justify **your answer.
parts.solution_md:
Having a high level of non-current liabilities, like long-term loans and mortgages, can help a growing business. These loans provide money to buy new equipment or buildings **[K]**. This can mean more products and potentially higher profits can be made. Also, the interest paid on these loans might reduce the amount of tax the business has to pay **[An]**

However, high non-current liabilities can be risky. Big loan payments **[K]** can make it hard for the business to pay its bills, especially if sales do not grow as expected, which is likely to mean that suppliers will no longer provide raw materials and goods, disrupting production **[An]**

Overall, I think high non-current liabilities are not always bad for growing businesses **[E]**. The chance to grow and make more money often makes up for the risks, as long as the business is careful about managing its debt and makes sure it can always make its loan payments **[E]**

> **[mark-scheme]**
> - You are writing a mini-argument with a decision
> 
>   - Give one relevant reason to support your view → 1 K mark
>   - Explain why this reason helps the business (cause-effect chain) →  1 An mark
>   - Give a different possible reason or viewpoint → 1 K mark
>   - Explain why this could also help the business → 1 An mark
>   - Make a decision — which argument is stronger or more important overall? → up to 2 E marks
> 
> **Mark scheme**
> 
> - Points might include
> 
>   - Non-current liabilities provide long-term finance [k] → loans and mortgages allow a business to invest in equipment or property to increase capacity and output [an]
>   - Borrowing can support growth [k] → allowing the business to take on more customers, produce more goods, and generate higher profits in the future [an]
>   - Interest on loans may reduce tax [k] → as interest payments are often tax-deductible, lowering the amount of corporation tax due [an]
>   - High liabilities increase financial risk [k] → if sales do not grow as expected, loan repayments could become difficult, potentially leading to cash flow problems or supplier issues [an]
>   - Debt reduces flexibility [k] → as regular repayments reduce the amount of cash available for other opportunities or unexpected costs [an]
> - Supported judgement might include
> 
>   - high non-current liabilities are acceptable if the business has a strong cash flow, reliable forecasts, and good debt management strategies [e]
>   - Not always a problem [e] → borrowing can be beneficial if the returns from growth exceed the costs of the debt [e]

Buildings **[K]**

Machinery **[K]**

parts.problem_md:
**State **whether each of the following is classified as a current asset or a current liability:

- Overdraft
- Trade receivables
- Trade payables
- Cash in bank
parts.solution_md:
An overdraft is a current liability **[K]**

Trade receivables are current assets **[K]**

Trade payables are current liabilities **[K]**

The total sum of money invested into a  company **[K]** by its owners **[K]**
